Value of the means of production.

Unpaid value that capital produces and that, when re-invested, becomes new capital.
Total product beyond what workers consume, split between capital and revenue.
The worker's capacity to work, sold as a commodity.
Labour performed beyond the value of wages; the source of surplus-value.
Re-investment of surplus-value as new capital; the reproduction of the capital relation on a larger scale.
Fusing of existing capitals into fewer hands; does not require growth of total wealth.
Growth of individual capitals through accumulation.

Workers in excess of capital's average needs, produced by accumulation itself.
Three forms of relative surplus population: factory, rural, and domestic-industry workers.

Wages, treated as the dependent variable of accumulation.
Initial accumulation in the transition from handicraft; the historical starting point.
Lever of centralisation that draws scattered money into capitalist hands.
Periodic phases of activity, high pressure, crisis and stagnation.
Incidental costs, such as pauperism, that capital pushes onto workers.
